Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.utils.taskscheduler

Class CronExpression

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.utils.taskscheduler.CronExpression
public final class CronExpression extends Object
A parser and evaluator for crontab-style schedules, the timing core of the desktop TaskScheduler. It understands the classic five-field form 
  minute  hour  day-of-month  month  day-of-week
and, for sub-minute jobs, the six-field form that prefixes a seconds field 
  second  minute  hour  day-of-month  month  day-of-week

Each field accepts * (any), ? (any, day fields), a single value, an inclusive range a-b, a step *&#47;n or a-b/n or a/n, and a comma-separated list of any of those. Months and week-days also accept their three-letter English names (JAN, MON), and week-day 7 is an alias for 0 (Sunday). The convenience macros @yearly, @annually, @monthly, @weekly, @daily, @midnight, @hourly and @minutely expand to the equivalent field expressions, and @reboot marks a job that runs once whenever the scheduler starts.

Following the Vixie-cron rule, when both the day-of-month and the day-of-week fields are restricted (neither is */?) a time matches if either one matches; otherwise the single restricted day field governs. Instances are immutable and thread-safe. All evaluation is pure and deterministic - the clock is passed in - so the whole grammar is unit testable headlessly.

    • nextFireTime

      public Optional<ZonedDateTime> nextFireTime(ZonedDateTime after)
      The next instant strictly after after at which this expression fires, or Optional.empty() if it never fires again within 5 years (e.g. an impossible date such as 30 February) or the expression is @reboot.

      For a five-field expression the result is always on a minute boundary (seconds zeroed); for a six-field expression it carries seconds.
